messages:
Alex (ACME-Netops): Hey team, our Redwood Private agents are failing to fetch model artifacts. Agent logs show repeated TLS handshake timeouts to artifacts.redwood-internal.com. Started after we rolled out a default-deny egress policy. Ticket TKT-4821. Any pointers?
Maya (Support): thanks Alex — can you paste the agent pod logs snippet and the exact NetworkPolicy/CNI egress rules you applied? Also which CNI (antrea/other) are you on?
Alex (ACME-Netops): We're on Antrea 1.7.0. Logs:
```
2024-04-15T14:02:10Z agent INFO fetching https://artifacts.redwood-internal.com/v1/models/foo: TLS handshake timeout
2024-04-15T14:02:20Z agent WARN retrying (5/10)
```
NetworkPolicy applied was namespace default-deny egress (egress: []), node-level iptables policy also enforces outbound only to corp-proxy.
Maya (Support): ok that explains it. Two common failure modes: 1) Antrea Egress (or namespace NP) blocking external 443, 2) host firewall / iptables blocking direct egress to artifact IPs. Can you exec into an agent pod and try a curl + openssl to confirm?
Alex (ACME-Netops): ran from agent pod (non-root):
```
# kubectl exec -n redwood-agent agent-abc -c agent -- curl -v https://artifacts.redwood-internal.com/v1/health --max-time 10
* Rebuilt URL to: https://artifacts.redwood-internal.com/v1/health
*   Trying 10.23.45.9...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* connect to 10.23.45.9 port 443 failed: Connection timed out
* Failed to connect to artifacts.redwood-internal.com port 443: Connection timed out
```
openssl s_client can't reach host either (timeout).
Sanjay (Eng): thanks — looks like L3/L4 egress is blocked before TLS. Could you run `kubectl get egress -n kube-system` and `kubectl get networkpolicy -A | grep deny`? Also node iptables: `sudo iptables -S | grep DROP` on a node.
Alex (ACME-Netops): Output:
```
$ kubectl get egress -A
No resources found.
$ kubectl get networkpolicy -A
default   default-deny-egress   2024-04-15   default   PolicyTypes: Egress   egress: []
$ sudo iptables -S | grep DROP
-A OUTPUT -m conntrack --ctstate NEW -j DROP
```
Sanjay (Eng): aha — host OUTPUT chain drops NEW connections (corporate host-level policy), and your NP removes pod-level egress. Agent traffic running in cluster can't establish new outbound TCP because node firewall drops it. Two remediation options: 1) add an exception on node firewall for the artifact IPs/CIDR or corporate proxy, or 2) configure the agent DaemonSet to use the corporate HTTP(S)_PROXY env to tunnel via proxy (recommended if you have enforced egress).
Maya (Support): If you prefer we can provide the minimal Antrea egress rule + DaemonSet patch to set proxy env vars. Which would you like to try first?
Alex (ACME-Netops): we'll try adding a NetworkPolicy exception first so pods can reach artifacts directly, since proxy is more change control. What exact NP rule would allow only agent pods to talk to artifacts over 443?
Sanjay (Eng): minimal NP (namespace scoped) you can apply in redwood-agent ns: allow egress to artifacts IP range on port 443 only for DaemonSet pods. Example (conceptual):
```
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: allow-redwood-artifacts
  namespace: redwood-agent
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: redwood-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 10.23.45.0/24    # artifacts IPs
    ports:
    - protocol: TCP
      port: 443
```
If you don't have static IPs for artifacts, you can allow to the corporate proxy IP instead.
Alex (ACME-Netops): applied NP above (replaced cidr with our artifact IP block). Restarted agent pods. Testing now...
Kai (Oncall Bot): deploy/agent rolling-restart started by Alex (ACME-Netops) — 3 pods restarting.
Alex (ACME-Netops): After restart, curl from agent pod now returns 200 and agent logs show successful model downloads.
```
2024-04-15T14:10:03Z agent INFO fetched model foo v2 (size 24MB) in 1.2s
```
Maya (Support): awesome, glad that fixed it 🎉 Would you like us to add a note to the tenant's runbook recommending either 1) add host firewall exceptions for Redwood artifact CIDRs or 2) set HTTP(S)_PROXY env on agent DaemonSet so it works behind corporate egress?
Alex (ACME-Netops): yes please add runbook note and include the example NP and the proxy env snippet. Closing TKT-4821. Thanks all.
Sanjay (Eng): noted — sending runbook snippet. Closing on our side.
Maya (Support): marking resolved. If you hit anything else ping us @support.
Alex (ACME-Netops): thanks everyone!
